summary: Chile admits most of Europe, North America, South America and much of Asia-Pacific visa-free for 90 days, and the old reciprocity fees charged to US, Canadian, Mexican and Australian visitors have all been abolished. Everyone else applies for a consular tourist visa; Venezuelan and Haitian citizens have needed one since 2018–19.

passportValidity.text: Chile requires a passport valid for the duration of your stay, and does not impose a formal six-month rule on visa-exempt visitors. Airlines may still apply their own six-month policy, so allow a margin. Argentine, Brazilian, Uruguayan, Paraguayan, Bolivian, Peruvian, Ecuadorian and Colombian citizens can enter on a national identity card.

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not required to enter. Private clinics in Santiago expect payment up front, and rescue costs in Patagonia or the Atacama are high — cover including mountain rescue is worth having.

declarations.name: Sworn agricultural declaration (Declaración Jurada SAG)
declarations.text: Every arriving traveler must complete a sworn declaration for the agricultural service (SAG) stating whether they carry food, plants, seeds, wood or animal products. It can be filed online before arrival or on the form handed out on the flight. Undeclared items — including fruit taken from the plane — carry fines that can run into hundreds of US dollars.

declarations.name: Tarjeta Única Migratoria (TUM)
declarations.text: The tourist card issued at the border is now electronic. Download or photograph your TUM after entry — hotels use it to exempt foreign visitors from VAT on accommodation paid in foreign currency, and you may be asked for it on departure.

currencyLimits.text: Cash or negotiable instruments of USD 10,000 or more must be declared to customs on arrival and departure.

notes: Chile's agricultural border controls are among the strictest anywhere: no fresh fruit, vegetables, seeds, honey, meat, dairy or untreated wood, including items bought in the airport of departure.
The same controls apply on internal crossings into Region XV and the far north and south, and on flights to Easter Island.
Foreign visitors paying a hotel in US dollars with a foreign card are exempt from the 19% VAT. Show your passport and TUM at check-in.

payments.text: Chile is close to cashless in cities: cards and contactless work almost everywhere, including buses in Santiago via a Bip! card. Carry pesos for Patagonian villages, small markets and rural buses. ATM withdrawal fees are high. Take out larger amounts less often.

safety.text: Chile remains one of the safer countries in South America, but street crime in central Santiago, Valparaíso and around bus terminals has risen noticeably — pickpocketing, phone snatching and distraction thefts are the main risks. Earthquakes are frequent and the country is well prepared; learn the tsunami evacuation routes on the coast.

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to March is the southern summer — the only sensible window for Torres del Paine and the Lake District. The Atacama works year-round, and June to September is ski season in the Andes near Santiago.

idp.text: Chile is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: Do not carry any food across a Chilean border, including an apple from the plane. The agricultural declaration is compulsory, sniffer dogs work the baggage hall, and fines for an undeclared item start in the hundreds of dollars.

Easter Island (Rapa Nui) has its own entry rules: stays are capped at 30 days, and you must show a return ticket, a booking with a registered hotel or a letter from a Rapa Nui host, and file the Rapa Nui entry form before boarding. Book accommodation before you book the flight.

Foreign visitors are exempt from Chile's 19% VAT on hotel stays when paying in US dollars with a foreign card or cash. Present your passport and electronic TUM at check-in. Many hotels will not apply it unless you ask.

Citizens of Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia can enter Chile on a national identity card instead of a passport under the regional agreement — useful for overland border hops.
Chile is over 4,000 km long. Santiago to Punta Arenas is a four-hour flight, and the Atacama and Patagonia are effectively different trips. Plan domestic flights rather than buses for the long legs.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Chile?
faq.answer: Most visitors do not. Citizens of the EU and Schengen states, the UK, Ireland, the US, Canada, Mexico, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Israel, Singapore, South Africa and virtually all of South and Central America enter visa-free for up to 90 days as tourists. Everyone else applies for a consular tourist visa at a Chilean consulate before traveling.

faq.question: Is there still a reciprocity fee to enter Chile?
faq.answer: No. Chile phased out the arrival reciprocity charges it once levied on US, Canadian, Mexican and — last of all — Australian visitors; the Australian fee ended in 2020. There is nothing to pay on arrival for visa-exempt travelers.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Chile?
faq.answer: Ninety days as a tourist. One extension of up to a further 90 days can be requested from the Servicio Nacional de Migraciones for a fee of roughly USD 100, and it must be applied for before your current permission expires. Repeatedly leaving and re-entering to reset the clock is treated as abuse and can lead to a shortened stamp.

faq.question: Are there extra rules for visiting Easter Island?
faq.answer: Yes. Rapa Nui limits visitors to 30 days and requires a return ticket, a reservation with a registered tourist establishment or an invitation from a Rapa Nui resident, and a completed entry form submitted before departure. The mainland agricultural rules also apply on the flight over.

faq.question: What is the SAG declaration?
faq.answer: It is Chile's compulsory sworn declaration about food, plants, seeds, wood and animal products, filed online before arrival or on the form handed out in flight. Chile protects a disease-free agricultural sector and enforces this seriously. An undeclared piece of fruit is a fine, not a warning.

faq.question: Do Venezuelan or Haitian citizens need a visa for Chile?
faq.answer: Yes. Chile introduced a consular tourist visa requirement for Haitian citizens in 2018 and for Venezuelan citizens in 2019, and both remain in force. Apply at a Chilean consulate well before travel, as processing can be slow.
